newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's ruling Islamists in bid to save coalition.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's ruling Islamists in bid to save coalition.

text.p: Turkey's ruling Islamists on Thursday began a race against time to save their shaky coalition from bursting apart under the strain of criticism from the staunchly secularist army.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan held four hours of talks with a rightist powerbroker and coalition partner Tansu Ciller, whose conservative True Path Party has threatened to pull out of the coalition within a week.

"We have openly put forward a solution," Ciller, who was Turkey's first woman prime minister, told reporters after meeting Erbakan. "The solution is democracy, the supremacy of the people's will," she said.

True Path, a pro-Western party, said on Wednesday night it would withdraw from the government if Ciller, now the foreign minister, was not made prime minister by June 18 under a plan to deflect criticism of the alliance by the influential generals.

Investors were scared off by the latest political uncertainty in Turkey, which has not had a stable government since a right-left coalition collapsed in 1995. Istanbul stocks dropped 1.99 percent at the close of trading, brokers said.
The current government has been hamstrung by disputes over religious activism since the army called in February for a crackdown on Moslem revivalism.
"This government has stopped being effective," the Hurriyet daily on Thursday quoted Ciller as telling her party MPs.
Erbakan, NATO member Turkey's first Islamist leader, is to transfer power to Ciller by the end of this month under a government plan for snap elections to try to resolve the army dispute.

But no date has been fixed for early polls and the coalition allies disagree on the timing of the handover. It would also have to be approved by the president and parliament, where Erbakan lacks an absolute majority.
The resignation of an MP from Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party weakened the coalition's position further on Thursday, leaving it with 274 MPs in the 550-seat assembly, where two seats are vacant.
Welfare deputy Ertugrul Yalcinbayir said in a statement to announce his resignation that he would act as an independent MP.

Far-right leader Muhsin Yazicioglu, whose small Grand Unity Party has eight MPs, joined the talks with Ciller and Erbakan in a possible sign the government was searching for a third coalition partner to boost it in the national assembly.

Yazicioglu denied he had discussed details of the planned power transfer. "I am not taking on our agenda any of this stuff about an election law, an election date or entering the government," he told reporters.

A leading member of Erbakan's Welfare Party called on Ciller to stay in the 11-month-old alliance. "There is no reason to pull out of the government at the moment," party deputy chairman Ahmet Tekdal told a news conference.
The True Path pullout threat was issued only hours after the military urged ordinary Turks on Wednesday to fight the danger of Islamic activism.

"It is the main duty of every secularist and democratic citizen who loves his country...not to stand neutral and to act against the increasing reactionary threat," General Fevzi Turkeri said at an army briefing for reporters on resurgent Islamism.

The top brass used some of its strongest anti-Islamist language yet at the briefing. Turkeri reminded reporters that the army's role was to protect the country "by force of arms" from domestic and external threats.
The Turkish media took the comment as a warning that the army is willing to use force against the Islamists.
"About the only thing they didn't say was that they are taking over the civilian administration," columnist Mehmet Ali Birand wrote in the Sabah daily.
Close Erbakan aide Abdullah Gul failed to appear as scheduled for a meeting in Istanbul between senior bureaucrats from eight Moslem countries, apparently due to the political crisis.
Leader and officials from the Moslem group, known as the Developing-Eight (D-8), are to hold their first summit in the city this weekend. The group's formation was the brainchild of Erbakan. R
